identity.name: Sai (Eighteen Kingdoms)
alt_names: Sai, one of the Three Qins

land.text: the Qin heartland given to Sima Xin: 'northeastern Shaanxi' (Eighteen Kingdoms table); 'the lands of the former Qin state in the Guanzhong region' (Sima Xin page)

predecessors.note: One of the Three Qins with yong and zhai, given by Xiang Yu to the Qin general Sima Xin in 206 BC.

land.text: Sima Xin's kingdom: 'Defeated by Liu Bang' (Eighteen Kingdoms table)

successors.note: The surrender is 205 on the Chu-Han Contention page and 206 on the Sima Xin page; the kingdom-of-han dossier (ea-01) gains Sai in 205.

capitals.name: Yueyang (Yanliang, Xi'an)
capitals.note: NOT CONFIRMED. The Sima Xin page names Yueyang only as his earlier posting and the place his head was displayed, not as a capital; neither the Eighteen Kingdoms table nor any page opened gives Sai a capital. Yueyang is the traditional seat, in the Guanzhong east of Xianyang, 330 km south of the Cliopatria outline's centre.

correction.text: the Kingdom of Sai: 'northeastern Shaanxi' (Eighteen Kingdoms table); the 41 of the shape's 86 cells that lie across the Yellow River in Shanxi are dropped

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 16,521 km2 outline (86 grid cells, lat 36.7-38.6 N) agrees with the table's 'northeastern Shaanxi' only in part: 45 cells lie in Shaanxi and 41 across the Yellow River in Shanxi, which no page gives to Sai, so the Shanxi cells are dropped. The Sima Xin page puts Sai in 'the Guanzhong region' with the other two Qins, which is further south than the table's northeast; no page opened separates the three kingdoms' lands, so the outline is kept as the table's reading and flagged. The years change: 206-205, not to 204. No area to compare.

region.text: the Kingdom of Sai: 'northeastern Shaanxi' (Eighteen Kingdoms table); the 41 of the shape's 86 cells that lie across the Yellow River in Shanxi are dropped

ledger.note: 206: Xiang Yu makes Sima Xin King of Sai. The Eighteen Kingdoms were 'created by military leader Xiang Yu in 206 BCE'; the table has Sai, Sima Xin (Qin general), 'northeastern Shaanxi'; the Sima Xin page: 'were made the rulers of three of the Eighteen Kingdoms' and 'occupied the lands of the former Qin state in the Guanzhong region'. The year is the page's; the outline is the researcher's reading of the table (Shaanxi cells of the Cliopatria shape).

region.text: the Kingdom of Sai: 'northeastern Shaanxi' (Eighteen Kingdoms table); the 41 of the shape's 86 cells that lie across the Yellow River in Shanxi are dropped

ledger.note: 205: Sima Xin surrenders and Sai passes to Liu Bang. Chu-Han Contention page: 'Sima Xin, the King of Sai, Dong Yi, the King of Di, and Shen Yang, the King of Henan, surrendered to Liu Bang' (205 BCE, no month); the Eighteen Kingdoms table: 'Defeated by Liu Bang'. The Sima Xin page dates it 206 ('Later that year', after Liu Bang's forces captured Zhang Han's kingdom); 205 follows the Chu-Han page, the Zhang Han page (Feiqiu fell in June or July 205) and the kingdom-of-han and zhai dossiers. Page silent on commanderies set up afterwards.

region.text: the Kingdom of Sai: 'northeastern Shaanxi' (Eighteen Kingdoms table); the 41 of the shape's 86 cells that lie across the Yellow River in Shanxi are dropped

ledger.note: 205: the Kingdom of Sai ends with Sima Xin's surrender. He later 'defected to Xiang Yu after Liu Bang's defeat at Pengcheng' (205) and killed himself in 204 after Chenggao (Sima Xin page), holding no land again on any page.

wars.name: Liu Bang's conquest of the Three Qins
wars.outcome: Liu Bang's army defeated Zhang Han; Sima Xin and Dong Yi surrendered; the Guanzhong became Han's base.
wars.note: No ground is named for Sai itself, so no contest zone is drawn; the Sima Xin page dates the surrender 206, the Chu-Han Contention page 205. The fighting zone is Yong's (see the yong dossier).

certainty.note: 'Northeastern Shaanxi' is the only description of the land on the table; the Sima Xin page says only 'the Guanzhong region'.

sources.title: Eighteen Kingdoms
sources.note: The table of the eighteen kingdoms: Yong, Sai, Di, Yin and the others, with kings and modern territories; created by Xiang Yu in 206 BC; no capitals, no dates of fate.

sources.title: Sima Xin
sources.note: King of Sai 206 BC; surrendered to Liu Bang 'later that year' (206); defected to Xiang Yu 205; died 204.

sources.title: Chu-Han Contention
sources.note: Dated 205 BC for the conquest of the Three Qins, the surrender of Sima Xin, Dong Yi and Shen Yang, the attack on Henei in April-May 205, Feiqiu July-August 205.

notes: Cliopatria's Sai row (206-204) is cut to 206-205 (surrender: 205 on the Chu-Han Contention page, 206 on the Sima Xin page; 205 follows the group: kingdom-of-han and zhai have it). Wikidata Q5349053 is the Eighteen Kingdoms item shared by twelve rows; each is its own kingdom, none merged. Pages opened: Eighteen Kingdoms, Sima Xin, Chu-Han Contention (3 against a budget of 1-2; the third settles the 205/206 conflict). The outline is the Shaanxi part of Cliopatria's shape. KNOWN WEAKNESS: the table says 'northeastern Shaanxi' but the Sima Xin page says Guanzhong; the real partition of Guanzhong among the Three Qins (Sai east of Xianyang, Yong west, Zhai north) is not on any page opened, and the capital Yueyang lies outside the drawn outline. A gap-filler should open the Qin or Chu-Han pages that name the commanderies each king received. No infobox area to compare with 16,521 km2.
